package_info.why_malicious: These versions were compromised to include code that prompts users to connect their cryptocurrency wallets, enabling phishing attacks and theft of digital assets. The malicious code was injected into the main distributable file and distributed via npm and CDNs, targeting end-users of websites embedding the library.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when the lottie-player component is loaded in the browser)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Displays a popup to the user prompting them to connect their cryptocurrency wallet (e.g., MetaMask, Exodus, Coinbase) when the component is loaded on a website.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code injects a UI element that aggressively solicits sensitive wallet connections from users, which is not part of the legitimate functionality of an animation player.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A normal animation player should not interact with cryptocurrency wallets or prompt for financial credentials. The presence of wallet connection prompts is a clear deviation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate dApps or crypto-related sites may prompt for wallet connections, but not a generic animation library.
key_indicators: UI elements referencing popular crypto wallets
Event listeners triggering wallet connection prompts
References to wallet SDKs in a non-crypto package

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after user interacts with the wallet popup)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After the user attempts to connect their wallet, the code exfiltrates sensitive wallet information to an external attacker-controlled endpoint.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating wallet data to an external server is a classic phishing and credential theft technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate animation library should never transmit user wallet data to third-party servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate wallet integrations may communicate with official wallet APIs, but not arbitrary external endpoints.
key_indicators: Network requests to non-official, suspicious domains
POST requests containing wallet or credential data
No user consent or legitimate reason for data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: User visits a website embedding the compromised lottie-player component.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code in the component is loaded and executed in the user's browser.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code displays a popup prompting the user to connect their cryptocurrency wallet.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is tricked into interacting with the wallet connection UI.

attack_chain.action: If the user attempts to connect their wallet, the code captures wallet information.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive wallet data is exfiltrated to an attacker-controlled server.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses stolen wallet credentials to initiate unauthorized transactions, resulting in financial theft.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: theft of cryptocurrency assets.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected wallet connection popups from non-crypto libraries
Network requests to unknown or suspicious domains after wallet interaction
Inclusion of wallet SDKs or references in unrelated packages
file_indicators: dist/lottie-player.js containing wallet-related code or references
Presence of minified code with wallet UI elements in animation libraries
network_indicators: Outbound POST requests to domains not associated with official wallet providers
Connections to attacker-controlled endpoints after user interaction
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for JavaScript libraries (especially animation or UI components) that display wallet connection prompts or reference wallet SDKs. Analyze network traffic for unexpected outbound requests to non-official domains following user interaction with such popups. Use static analysis to detect wallet-related code in packages where it is not expected. Alert on any animation library that attempts to access or transmit wallet information.
